1.explanation: This example creates 650 data-rows so that, with a fixed pageSize of 10, you end up with 65 pages. In Carbon v9’s Pagination (which the security add-ons wrap in a DataTablePagination component), the page‐number picker is rendered as a standard `<Select>` with one `<option>` per page. Clicking it opens a very long dropdown that overflows the viewport—exactly as shown in your screenshot. Scrolling the oversized list is required to reach high page numbers, reproducing the bad UX.
1.bug_scenario: In the DataTablePagination story (or directly using Carbon’s v9 `Pagination` component), when you load a data-table with ~650 rows and fix the page size to 10, you end up with 65 pages. Because the component renders the page selector as a `<Select>` with one `<option>` per page, clicking the control produces a dropdown that stretches well beyond the browser viewport. The user must scroll inside the oversized list to find and pick page 60 (or any high-numbered page), which is a bad experience.
